reports.report_text: During a crane lifting operation, a worker entered the designated lifting zone while a heavy valve assembly was suspended approximately 6 metres above ground level. The worker was standing directly beneath the suspended load, within the potential line of fire. The lifting area had not been effectively barricaded and the exclusion zone was not being maintained. The operator stopped the lifting operation after noticing the worker and the worker moved away from the suspended load. No injury occurred, but an uncontrolled release or dropped load could have resulted in fatal or serious injury.

reports.report_text: During maintenance on a hydrocarbon process line, a welding crew was preparing to start hot work on the line. The line had not been positively isolated or locked out from the energy source, and hydrocarbon residue was still present inside the line. reports.report_text: During scheduled maintenance on a pressurized hydrocarbon condensate transfer line at Moran Central Tank Farm, a contract maintenance crew commenced hot work cutting operations without executing positive mechanical isolation (blind spade installation) or lockout/tagout (LOTO). Residual flammable condensate and hydrocarbon vapor were detected inside the pipe spool during inspection after hot work sparks ignited an adjacent hydrocarbon weep. The required continuous gas monitoring and combustible gas test had not been performed prior to hot work permit issuance. The hot work was immediately shut down. Major fire and explosion potential existed with credible fatality risk.

The crew was about to begin welding when the unsafe condition was identified and the activity was stopped. The situation had the potential to cause a major fire or explosion, resulting in serious injury or fatality.

Sample Safety Report – Energy Isolation Near Miss

Report Type: Near MissDate: 05 September 2026Site: Oil Processing FacilityDepartment: Maintenance

Safety Observation Report

During scheduled maintenance on a centrifugal pump at the oil processing facility, a maintenance technician was assigned to inspect and replace a damaged coupling guard.

Before starting the work, the technician isolated the electrical supply to the pump from the local control panel. However, during verification, the maintenance supervisor identified that the pump could still be started remotely from the central control room.

The remote electrical control circuit had not been isolated as part of the energy isolation procedure.

While the technician was preparing to remove the coupling guard, an operator in the control room attempted to start the pump as part of a routine operational check. The pump did not start because another protective interlock prevented operation.

The technician was positioned close to the rotating equipment at the time. If the protective interlock had failed or been bypassed, the unexpected startup of the pump could have resulted in serious injury.

No injury occurred.

Hazard Identified

Unexpected energization and startup of rotating equipment.

Potential Consequences

Serious crush injury 

Entanglement with rotating equipment 

Severe hand or body injury 

Barrier Failure

Incomplete energy isolation 

Remote control circuit was not isolated 

Isolation verification was insufficient before maintenance began 

Immediate Action Taken

The maintenance activity was stopped immediately. The supervisor informed the control room, and a complete isolation procedure was performed.

The electrical supply and remote control circuit were isolated, locked, and verified before maintenance resumed.

Recommended Follow-up Actions

Review the Lockout/Tagout procedure for rotating equipment. 

Ensure all energy sources, including remote and stored energy sources, are identified. 

Require verification of zero-energy state before maintenance begins. 

Conduct a toolbox talk on energy isolation and unexpected equipment startup.

Report Type: Near MissLocation: Pump Maintenance Area – Process Plant

During the scheduled maintenance of a centrifugal pump, the maintenance team was assigned to inspect and replace a damaged coupling guard. Before starting the work, the team stopped the pump using the normal control switch. However, the electrical supply to the motor was not physically isolated and no lockout/tagout procedure was applied.

One technician began inspecting the coupling area while another worker was preparing tools nearby. During the inspection, the pump unexpectedly started when the control system received an automatic restart signal following a temporary power interruption.

The technician immediately noticed movement in the rotating equipment and stepped away from the pump. No injury occurred, but the technician had been standing very close to the rotating coupling and could have been struck or caught in the moving machinery.

The supervisor stopped the equipment and the electrical supply was subsequently isolated. The investigation found that the required energy isolation and lockout procedure had not been completed before maintenance began. The team had relied only on the normal stop button and had not verified that the equipment was in a zero-energy state.

The incident was recorded as a near miss because no one was injured. However, the uncontrolled release of energy and unexpected movement of rotating equipment had the potential to cause a serious injury or fatality.

Report Type: Near MissDate: 05 September 2026Site: Oil Processing FacilityDepartment: Maintenance

Safety Observation Report

During scheduled maintenance on a centrifugal pump at the oil processing facility, a maintenance technician was assigned to inspect and replace a damaged coupling guard.

Before starting the work, the technician isolated the electrical supply to the pump from the local control panel. However, during verification, the maintenance supervisor identified that the pump could still be started remotely from the central control room.

The remote electrical control circuit had not been isolated as part of the energy isolation procedure.

While the technician was preparing to remove the coupling guard, an operator in the control room attempted to start the pump as part of a routine operational check. The pump did not start because another protective interlock prevented operation.

The technician was positioned close to the rotating equipment at the time. If the protective interlock had failed or been bypassed, the unexpected startup of the pump could have resulted in serious injury.

No injury occurred.

Hazard Identified

Unexpected energization and startup of rotating equipment.

Potential Consequences

Serious crush injury 

Entanglement with rotating equipment 

Severe hand or body injury 

Barrier Failure

Incomplete energy isolation 

Remote control circuit was not isolated 

Isolation verification was insufficient before maintenance began 

Immediate Action Taken

The maintenance activity was stopped immediately. The supervisor informed the control room, and a complete isolation procedure was performed.

The electrical supply and remote control circuit were isolated, locked, and verified before maintenance resumed.

Recommended Follow-up Actions

Review the Lockout/Tagout procedure for rotating equipment. 

Ensure all energy sources, including remote and stored energy sources, are identified. 

Require verification of zero-energy state before maintenance begins. 

Conduct a toolbox talk on energy isolation and unexpected equipment startup.

Report Type: Near MissDate: 05 September 2026Site: Moran Tank FarmDepartment: Operations

Safety Observation Report

During a maintenance activity at the Moran Tank Farm, a contractor team was preparing to inspect a process line located approximately 6 metres above ground level.

The workers accessed the elevated platform using a temporary ladder. During the inspection, it was observed that one worker was working close to an unprotected edge without being properly connected to an approved fall-arrest anchorage point.

The worker was wearing a safety harness; however, the lanyard was not attached to any secure anchorage. The temporary work platform also did not have complete edge protection on one side.

While attempting to inspect the pipeline, the worker lost balance momentarily after stepping on a loose section of the platform. Another worker nearby assisted him, preventing a potential fall.

No injury occurred.

Immediate Hazard Identified

Potential fall from height resulting in serious injury or fatality.

Barrier Failure

Fall protection system was not properly connected. 

Incomplete edge protection was present. 

Temporary work platform inspection was inadequate before work started. 

Immediate Action Taken

The activity was stopped immediately. The worker was moved to a safe location, and the supervisor was informed. The temporary platform was isolated until proper edge protection and approved anchorage points could be verified.

Recommended Follow-up

Inspect all temporary elevated work platforms. 

Verify fall-protection anchorage before work begins. 

Conduct a toolbox talk on working-at-height requirements. 

Review supervisor pre-job inspection procedures.
